lines.trans: Arkady Borisovich, we are your lawyers from Moscow.

words.gram: patronymic (son of Boris), used as address

lines.trans: Good afternoon, gentlemen! I've been waiting for you. Come in, please.

words.gram: nominative singular, masculine; добрый день = good afternoon
nominative plural, masculine, used as address

lines.trans: Look what the conditions are like here. Into this room, please.
Hello, Ilya Olegovich.

words.gram: patronymic (son of Oleg), used as address

lines.trans: Excuse me, who are you? What is this?
I am the lawyer Mishkin, I'm handling this case.
Here is an order from the prosecutor's office. The hearing will be this evening.
What do you mean, this evening? That's impossible!
We have already made a decision on this case. A review is only in two months.
The prosecutor's office thinks otherwise. There are many serious mistakes in the case.
We demand that house arrest be replaced. What's needed is a travel ban.
Do you think that's really possible?
There is no reason to keep you under arrest. Today you will walk out of here.

words.gloss: will walk out, will get out

lines.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.
My angels, this is for you! An old Soviet habit.

words.gram: nominative plural, masculine, used as address

lines.trans: Goodbye, Arkady Borisovich.

words.gram: genitive singular, neuter; до свидания = goodbye
